author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. Read-only, reachable only by its own address.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every one is listed under its stored name, all on one page
given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the specialty directory is opened, then each of them is shown under it by first name then last name
given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown under each of them
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is not shown
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then it is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it
given a clinic that knows no specialty at all, when the specialty directory is opened, then an empty directory is shown rather than a failure
given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no link to the specialty directory
non_goals: a navigation entry, or a link from any other page, to the specialty directory
managing veterinarians or their specialties — NG-2 is unchanged
paging the specialty directory; every specialty renders on one page
searching or filtering the specialty directory
changing the existing paged veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001)
notes: Owner quoted the page's address in the intake (handoff line 1): "GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it." Ordering is unstated by the owner; I set stable order, mirroring the existing directory's edge case 1, and left the ordering key to design. Any new user-facing wording this page needs binds REQ-LANG-002 — no hard-coded text, and present in every supported language bundle. NG-9 tension recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md: NG-9 declines searching for a veterinarian, and this page answers the inverse lookup as a fixed listing with no search, no filter, and no query — the narrowest reading consistent with the request. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No new domain term resolved: veterinarian and specialty, with the inverse relation, already sit in docs/ubiquitous-language.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory lives in the existing vet feature package and needs one thing the codebase does not have: the inverse of the Vet-to-Specialty relation. No type carries it, and Specialty has no repository, so specialties no veterinarian holds are unreachable today. Three new types in org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet: SpecialtyRepository (mirrors PetTypeRepository, returning every specialty in stored-name order), SpecialtyDirectory (immutable read model built by a pure static factory from the two repository results), and SpecialtyController (GET /specialties.html, binds no request input). docs/adr/2026-09-17-read-model-for-cross-entity-pages.md records why the inversion sits in a read model rather than in the controller or a new service layer, and docs/system-design.md Contracts carries the three rows plus the unlinked-page invariant. Package structure, dependency direction, and the no-service-layer shape are unchanged; vet still depends only on model.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request input: no request parameter, no path variable, no command object. The only bound argument is the framework-supplied Model. Nothing reaches a persisted type, so no allow-list is needed

Repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests: hand-written doubles implementing SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository, registered through a @TestConfiguration on the @WebMvcTest slice. Both interfaces are small enough to implement by hand, so the testing brief's real-or-hand-written-first rule applies. Do not copy VetControllerTests' @MockitoBean into the new class
Framework transport boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (testing-principles.md, mocking policy)
SpecialtyDirectoryTests crosses no boundary: real Vet and Specialty instances, no double. This is where the six acceptance criteria about grouping, ordering, and omission are proven

Acceptance criterion 7 (no page links to the directory) is proven by a test walking src/main/resources/templates and asserting no th:href resolves to /specialties.html, following I18nPropertiesSyncTest's file-walk precedent
SpecialtyController reads VetRepository.findAll(), which passes through the existing 'vets' JCache. No new cache is declared and CacheConfiguration is untouched

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository returning every row in name order via an explicit @Query; SpecialtyRepository copies this shape
GET handler that fills the Model and returns a view name; SpecialtyController copies this shape without the paging helper
page template delegating to the shared layout fragment; the specialty page reuses it and passes a menu value matching no navigation entry
resource-walking test over src/main; the no-link assertion follows it

risks.risk: Matching veterinarians to specialties by object equality or by name. BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so equality is identity: inside one persistence context the same row yields the same instance and the bug hides, while the @WebMvcTest doubles hand out distinct instances and it surfaces. The specialties table carries only an index on name, not a unique constraint, so two specialties may share a stored name
risks.mitigation: Match on getId(). SpecialtyDirectoryTests must include two distinct Specialty instances carrying the same id, and two specialties sharing a name (architecture-principles.md, Domain Core: aggregates reference each other by identity)

risks.risk: Assembling the inversion inside the controller, which the PRD's file_targets nudges toward. That places a domain relation's inversion in the web layer, where it is reachable only through MVC infrastructure
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory holds the inversion and the controller only delegates (architecture-principles.md, Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: holds no business rule; ADR 2026-09-17-read-model-for-cross-entity-pages)

risks.risk: Mapping an inverse @ManyToMany on Specialty to read the page from one query. Specialty is serialized inside the /vets representation that Vets roots, so an inverse side recurses there
risks.mitigation: Specialty stays unchanged; the relation keeps its single owning side on Vet (ADR 2026-09-17-read-model-for-cross-entity-pages, option 4 rejected)

risks.risk: New hard-coded page text, or a new message key added to only some bundles. I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on either
risks.mitigation: The page needs no new key: specialties, name, vets, and none are already present in all eleven bundles. Any key the implementer does add lands in all eleven (REQ-LANG-002)

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to the new repository read. The 'vets' cache has no eviction configured and that gap is an open question in docs/system-design.md
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository declares no cache; it carries @Transactional(readOnly = true) only

risks.risk: An empty clinic or an unheld specialty producing a failure rather than an empty rendering
risks.mitigation: The factory takes both collections as given and produces an entry per specialty with a possibly empty veterinarian list; the template renders an empty table when the directory has no entry (acceptance criteria 5 and 6)

notes:
Ordering, which the PRD left to design: specialties ascending by stored name, mirroring PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes() and Vet.getSpecialties(); veterinarians under each specialty by last name, then first name. Both orders are stable and neither was stated by the owner. OPEN QUESTION for a later product answer: the veterinarian order within a specialty is a design pick, not an owner decision. Displayed name is first name then last name, per the requirement, independent of the sort key.

Divergence from the prd-entry's file_targets, which are advisory: the handler goes in a new SpecialtyController rather than VetController. The owner package's three controllers set the one-controller-per-surface precedent, the naming rule prefixes a controller by the noun it serves, and VetController would otherwise take a second repository dependency for a page unrelated to the vet list. REQ-VET-001's paged vet list is untouched.

The layout fragment is reused as-is and gains no entry. Pass it a menu value matching none of its four fixed entries, so no navigation item is marked active for a page reachable only by its address.

NG-9 tension is already recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md and needs nothing from the implementer: this page is a fixed listing with no search box, no filter, and no query parameter. Keep it that way; adding either would cross into NG-9.

XSS: specialty names and veterinarian names render through th:text, which Thymeleaf escapes by default. Do not reach for th:utext.

No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge.

Effort rated involved: each piece has an adjacent seam to copy, but the read model has no precedent in this codebase and the identity-matching trap is easy to walk into.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No request input crosses the new boundary: SpecialtyController's only handler parameter is the framework-supplied Model (SpecialtyController.java:39-40, '@GetMapping("/specialties.html")' / 'public String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)'). A grep -F sweep of the vet package for '@ModelAttribute', '@RequestBody', '@RequestParam', '@PathVariable', 'InitBinder' returned only the pre-existing VetController.java:45 '@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page', so the new endpoint binds no persisted type and the mass-assignment row of docs/security-principles.md is not engaged.

Data access is a fixed JPQL string with no request-derived value: SpecialtyRepository.java:32 '@Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name")', annotated '@Transactional(readOnly = true)' (line 31) and exposing no write method, matching PetTypeRepository's shape. No concatenation, no parameter.

Output escaping stays on the framework default. Every value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text ('${entry.specialty.name}' line 20, '${veterinarian.firstName + \u0027 \u0027 + veterinarian.lastName}' line 23); the file contains no th:utext and no Thymeleaf preprocessing '__${...}__' expression (read in full, 30 lines). The menu argument passed to the layout fragment is the literal 'specialties' (line 4), not a model value, so the fragment's preprocessed th:href="@{__${link}__}" (fragments/layout.html:31) is still fed only literals from the call sites.

No new dependency and no build change: 'git status --porcelain build.gradle gradle*' returned empty, so the dependency-policy checks in docs/system-design.md are not engaged by this change. OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured in build.gradle (plugins block lists java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring boot 4.1.1, dependency-management, native, cyclonedx, javaformat, nohttp), so no NVD match ran in this review — that check is not run, not clean.

No credential, token, or unsafe randomness added: a case-insensitive grep -E over the three new main sources and both new test sources for 'password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|System.out|System.err|Random(' returned no match. No logging statement is added at all.

No shell, file, deserialization, or resource-path surface added: grep over the vet package for 'Runtime', 'ProcessBuilder', 'exec(', 'FileWriter', 'FileOutputStream', '/tmp/', 'JsonTypeInfo', 'enableDefaultTyping' returned no match. SpecialtyDirectory is a pure in-memory record built from the two repository results (SpecialtyDirectory.java:47-53) with no I/O.

The new read-only endpoint discloses nothing beyond the existing baseline: specialty names and veterinarian full names are already served by GET /vets.html and the GET /vets JSON resource (VetController.java:44, 64-70). Result size is bounded by table cardinality, not by caller input, matching the pre-existing unpaged findAll() at VetController.java:70 — no new unbounded-allocation path under attacker control.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Purely additive inside one module: four new files under the vet package plus a template, zero deletions and no edit to any existing production Java file, no build, config, schema, or sensitive path touched; the only new surface is one GET route that reads two repositories.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the whole of SpecialtyDirectory, the controller, the repository, and the template: the inversion keys on Specialty::getId rather than equals (deliberate, since BaseEntity overrides neither), holders are sorted once by last-then-first name before distribution so per-entry order is stable, an unheld specialty keeps an empty list, and every template value renders through th:text with no utext and no preprocessed expression.

test_adequacy.note: Nine unit tests over the real record assert whole-object equality and would fail on wrong order, a missed multi-specialty holder, an omitted unheld specialty, or name-collided specialties; the controller slice uses hand-written repository doubles and asserts rendered content, and the no-link criterion is a file walk over every template. The one untested branch is the template's none fallback for an unheld specialty, which mirrors the equally untested existing branch in vetList.html and resolves against a key present in the default bundle.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved with empty findings and empty recommendations, and every aspect names concrete evidence; I resolved four cited coordinates (SpecialtyController.java:39-40, SpecialtyDirectory.java:34/53/68, SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java:118/128, SpecialtyControllerTests.java:106) and each landed exactly where claimed. The security reviewer's note that OWASP Dependency-Check is unconfigured is a standing project gap on a change that touches no dependency, not a reservation.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions; the diff matches the design-block's primary paths, the page carries no navigation entry as the owner decided, and the NG-9 tension was recorded as a PRD open question rather than resolved, exactly as the intake instructed.

rationale: Additive slice: one new route, one new read model, no existing production file changed. The inversion reads correctly by identifier with stable ordering, tests assert real outcomes at both levels, and four clean approvals cite coordinates that resolve. A glance at the read model confirms it.
